title: JavaScript Array Methods You'll Use Daily
intro: These built-in methods replace most manual for-loops and make your code easier to read.

slides.heading: map()
slides.subtitle: Transform every item.
points: Returns a new array of the same length
examples: Users to a list of names

slides.heading: filter()
slides.subtitle: Keep only the matching items.
points: Keeps items where the callback returns true

slides.heading: find()
slides.subtitle: Get the first match.
examples: Looking up a user by ID

slides.heading: reduce()
slides.subtitle: Boil an array down to one value.
points: Carries an accumulator through each item

slides.heading: some() & every()
slides.subtitle: Yes-or-no questions about an array.
points: some: does at least one item match?

scenario.situation: An online store needs the total price of the in-stock items in a cart.
scenario.problem: A manual for-loop with if checks and a running total is long and easy to get wrong.
scenario.fix: cart.filter(i => i.inStock).reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0) does it in one readable line.
scenario.takeaway: Chain filter and reduce instead of hand-written loops.

cta: Which array method do you use the most?
